JUDGMENT
The petitioners No.1 to 3, have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Gaganashree.B.R., in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.09.2021.
SCCH4 3 MVC No.541/2022 2.

The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 19.09.2021 at about 6.00 p.m., the deceased Gaganashree, was pillion rider in Yamaha bike bearing Reg.No.KA40EE1901 with her villager by name Upendra with an intention to go her native place Banavathi from Pulaganahalli village, reached near Agrahara to Hosahalli village, at that time the rider drove the bike in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, without observing cow came on the road and the rider was immediately will control his vehicle and applied for break, for that the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on her head, bleeding injuries on her right ear and other parts of the body and the deceased was died on the spot.

Thereafter the deceased shifted to mortuary of Gowribidanur Government Hospital, on the next day i.e., on 20.09.2021 the doctors conducted post mortem over the dead body and handed SCCH4 4 MVC No.541/2022 over body to the petitioners.

The petitioners shifted the deceased in private vehicle for that the petitioner spent a more than Rs.20,000/ towards transportation expenses and the petitioners spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ towards funeral expenses.
The deceased was doing coolie and he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month,
he was contributing his entire income to his family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically, they have lost their bread earner.
The petitioner No.1 to 3 are the father, mother and husband of the deceased Gaganashree.B.R., have lost their beloved care taker.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ with interest.
SCCH4 5 MVC No.541/2022 3.

After service of notices the respondent No.2 did not appear, hence he placed Reddy B vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117190138/
2 exparte.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement contending that, there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.

That,
rider of the motor cycle did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
The deceased herself was perpetrator of the accident.
The insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further, denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation have claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Gaganashree.B.R. died in SCCH4 6 MVC No.541/2022 the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 19.09.2021 at about 6.00 p.m., near Agrahara Hosahalli village, Thondebavi Hobli, Gowribidanur Taluk,
due to the rash and negligence riding of the Yamaha motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA40EE1901 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependants of the deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the 2 nd petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
The respondent No.1 has examined its Assistant Managerclaims has examined as RW.1, through him got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to 3.
Further the Amnon Saxena, FDA Chikkaballapura RTO, Chikkaballapura has examined as RW.2, through him got marked document at Ex.R.4.
The respondent No.1 has filed memo to produced copy of reply notice marked at Ex.R.5.
SCCH4 7 MVC No.541/2022 6.
I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the material evidence that is available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1: In the affirmative,

3  Issue No.2 : In the affirmative.

sentences.text:
Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per the final orders  for the following.

REASONS ISSUE NO.1:
 8.

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, charge sheet, spot mahazar, IMV report,
spot sketch, Inquest report and PM report, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9 and 11.
9.

On going through the documents Nataraj who is brother of the deceased Gaganashree has lodged complaint with Manchenahalli police on 20.09.2021 alleging that, on 19.01.2021, he received a phone call SCCH4 8 MVC No.541/2022 from his brotherinlaw by name Gangaraju and he told that, Gagana and Upendra met with an accident.
Immediately, the complainant came and enquired with Gangaraju then he told that, complainant's sister Gagana and Upendra while proceeding on the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EE1901 on Agrahara, Hosahalli a cow came across the road, for that reason Upendra who was riding the motor cycle applied break suddenly.
Hence, the pillion rider Gaganashree fell from the bike and sustained injury near right ear and died on the spot, Upendra also sustained head injury.
10. Upon receiving the complaint the police have registered FIR against Upendra.
Thereafter, the police have visited the place of the accident and drawn spot mahazar and also seized the motor cycle involved in the accident.
The damages sustained to two wheeler involved in the accident is also noted in the IMV report.
The police SCCH4 9 MVC No.541/2022 have conducted Inquest.
As per the PM report the cause of death is due sub dural hemorrhage and traumatic brain injury.
The injuries found on the dead body of Gaganashree are also noted in the Inquest report as well as PM report.

11. As against the evidence of petitioner the respondent No.1 has examined its official namely Chaitresh.D Habbu as RW.1, through him authorization letter to give evidence, insurance policy and copy of notice issued to respondent No.2 along with postal acknowledgment are marked at Ex.R.1 to 3.
12.

The respondent No.1 has taken up defence that, the motor cycle which was ridden by Upendra S/o Venkatesh at the time of the accident has no valid and effective driving license to ride the motor cycle.
The respondent No.2 knowingly and willfully entrusted the SCCH4 10 MVC No.541/2022 motor cycle to the accused Upendra who did not possess driving license.
13. Though the respondent No.1 in the statement of objection denied the involvement of the insured vehicle the same is not come in the evidence of RW.1.

As such it is the defence of the respondent Reddy B vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117190138/
4 No.1 that, the owner of the insured vehicle has willfully handed over his vehicle to Upendra who did not possess the driving license to ride the motor cycle that means the RW.1 do not dispute the accident.

sentences.text: Except the liability.
14. The respondent No.2 is not contesting the claim petition.
During the course crossexamination of PW.1. nothing worth has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.

All the police records as well oral evidence of petitioner prove that, Gaganashree B.R. while proceeding as a pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing SCCH4 11 MVC No.541/2022 Reg.No.KA40EE1901 ridden by Upendra fell from the bike and Gaganashree died due to the accidental injuries.
15.
As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that, Gaganashree died in the accident dated 19.09.2021 which is caused by the driver of the Yamaha bike bearing Reg. No. KA40EE1901 which belonging to respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 16.
As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Gaganashree., died on 19.09.2021 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the respondent No.1.
As contended in the petition the petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is mother and petitioner No.3 is the husband of the deceased Gaganashree.B.R.,
The respondent does not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased Gaganashree.B.R.,.
The petitioners to prove their relationship, with the deceased Gaganashree.B.R., have produced notarized copies of their Aadhar cards of petitioner No.1 to 3 and TC of deceased.
These documents are marked at Ex.P.9.
The original documents of the notarized copies are also compared, during the course of evidence and found correct.
As per these documents the petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the husband of the deceased Gaganashree.B.R.,.
These documents are not disputed by the respondents.
The respondents has also not adduced rebuttal evidence.

In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the SCCH4 13 MVC No.541/2022 petitioners is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioners being the father,
mother and husband of the deceased, are the dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
18.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
As per the Transfer certificated marked at Ex.P.9, the date of birth of the deceased mentioned as 13.08.2005, the accident was occurred on 19.09.2021.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 16 years.

sentences.text: As stated in the petition deceased was doing coolie and she was earning Rs.15,000/per month.
In this regard the petitioners have not produced any documents.
it is found that deceased completed 10th SCCH4 14 MVC No.541/2022 class education just one year before the accident.
In this back ground it appears that deceased was not earning person.
However, the petitioners are entitle for compensation.

Hence, the income of deceased is considered notionally at Rs.14,000/ in the year 2021, then the annual income comes to Rs.1,68,000/.
20.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is '18'.
The future loss of income is Rs.30,24,000/.

Since the deceased left his father, mother and husband, it is considered that, there are three dependents of deceased, hence 1/3 rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.20,16,000/ (Rs.14,000/ X 12 X 18= Rs.30,24,000/ minus 1/3rd = Rs.10,08,000/).

In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

entities.text: Kirti and Another etc., V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Once notional income is determined, the effects of inflation would equally apply.
Further, no one would ever say that the improvements in skills that come with experience do not take place in the domain of work within the household.

It is worth nothing that, although not extensively discussed, this Court has been granting future prospects even in cases pertaining to notional income, as has been highlighted by my learned brother, Surya Kant,
J., in his opinion (Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654:
Sunita Tokas V. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2019) 20 SCC 688)".
SCCH4 17 MVC No.541/2022 Reddy B vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117190138/
6 23.

sentences.text:
As per the above decision, 40% of notional income should be added to total loss of dependency, to the age of deceased, which will be Rs.8,06,400/.
24.

The petitioner No.3 is the husband, hence I inclined to award a sum of Rs.44,000/ for loss of consortium. Rs.27,500/ towards loss of love and affection,
Rs.16,500/ towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/ towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
25.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 20,16,000/
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 8,06,400/
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/
4. Loss of love and affection Rs. 27,500/
5.

Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/
6. Transport of dead body Rs. 16,500/ Total Rs. 29,26,900/ SCCH4 18 MVC No.541/2022 26.
Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is bond to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:
27.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.29,26,900/
SCCH4 19 MVC No.541/2022 (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakhs Twenty Six Thousand and Nine Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.

The petitioner No.3 is the husband, hence I inclined to award a sum of Rs.44,000/ for loss of consortium. Rs.27,500/ towards loss of love and affection,
Rs.16,500/ towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/ towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
25.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 20,16,000/
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 8,06,400/
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/
4. Loss of love and affection Rs. 27,500/
5.

Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/
6. Transport of dead body Rs. 16,500/ Total Rs. 29,26,900/ SCCH4 18 MVC No.541/2022 26.
Hence, both the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is bond to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.29,26,900/
SCCH4 19 MVC No.541/2022 (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakhs Twenty Six Thousand and Nine Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 to 3 and are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 30:40:30.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.2, 50% shall be released to petitioner No.2 on her proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner No.1 and 3, it is ordered to release entire amount in their favour.
